newsitem.title: UK: UK extends compensation awards for water customers.
newsitem.headline: UK extends compensation awards for water customers.

text.p: The UK government on Monday extended compensation entitlements for customers of water companies to cover low water pressure with a payment of 25 stg.
Environment minister Robert Jones said customers would be entitled to 25 stg if they suffered two instances of low water pressure, each lasting more than an hour and both within any 28 day period.
The proposals come under the aegis of the Guaranteed Standards Scheme, which lays down recommended compensations for various failures in service by water companies.
Water industry regulator Ofwat welcomed the move, which followed its recommendation in May.
But Ofwat head Ian Byatt criticised the government for failing to implement his proposals on compensation in the event of using public standpipes for water supply.
"The government committed itself to introducing legislation as soon as parliamentary time allowed but we are seeing no progress," Byatt said in a statement.
"The government has failed to give sufficient priority to securing legal compensation for customers forced to use standpipes in the event of a drought order," Ofwat said.
